criteria: Parts (a) and (b) on both papers give brief, accurate, correctly targeted answers with no unnecessary explanation
Parts (c) on both papers develop two points fully, each with a reason or example
Parts (d)(i) on both papers explain two genuinely contrasting beliefs (Christian or Muslim as appropriate) and cite a specific, accurate source of wisdom and authority for each

Across both papers, uses accurate dates, names, scripture references and specialist religious terminology (Trinity, incarnation, sanctity of life, Tawhid, Akhirah, Jihad, Shari'ah) consistently and correctly, and correctly identifies where a non-religious (atheist or Humanist) viewpoint is required
exam_rubric.pass_threshold: A pass is a Grade-4-standard performance across both papers combined: accurate, well-selected AO1 knowledge of Christianity and Islam; developed 4-mark and 5-mark explanations, the 5-mark parts correctly citing a source of wisdom and authority for two genuinely contrasting beliefs; and, on both papers' extended evaluate questions, a balanced AO2 argument using religious and non-religious viewpoints that reaches a clearly justified conclusion, with acceptable SPaG on the two designated questions per paper.

source_notes: The specification names three Areas of Study (Religion and Ethics, Religion Peace and Conflict, Religion Philosophy and Social Justice), each offered with a choice of seven religions (Catholic Christianity, Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, Judaism, Sikhism); a candidate takes two of the three areas, each with one religion. This build itemises only the two chosen areas/religions in full; the third area and the unchosen religion options are recorded in declared_exclusions rather than itemised bullet by bullet, matching how unchosen options were handled for other rebuilt courses in this set.
Linked specification is Issue 2 (January 2024); the original meta_old.json carried over no source URLs from the earlier build, so these are newly located and recorded here.
